flow.zh: 從紐西蘭南島的 Christchurch，北上 Aoraki / Mt. Cook 國家公園數百公里，車行漫漫，沿途丘嶺延綿，斜坡草野，青翠欲滴。白色綿羊，時而散佈，時而成群，映照藍天，色澤鮮明。繼而遠山隨行，湖水點綴，浮雲淡泊飄逸，群樹隨風搖曳。黄昏時分抵達公園内的隱者客棧 ( Hermitage Inn )。暮色蒼茫裡，環顧山影朦朧，但見弦月孤懸天宇，寒凉四起，清寂無人見，不禁有 " 松下問童子，言師採藥去，只在此山中，雲深不知處 " 的蒼然。
flow.en: From Christchurch on New Zealand's South Island, we drove several hundred kilometers north to Aoraki / Mt. Cook National Park. The journey was long, the road winding past rolling hills and sloping meadows so green they seemed ready to drip. White sheep, now scattered, now gathered in flocks, stood out vividly against the reflected blue sky. Farther on, distant mountains kept pace alongside us, lakes dotted the landscape, clouds drifted light and unhurried, and stands of trees swayed in the wind. At dusk we arrived at the Hermitage Inn within the park. In the vast, hazy twilight, I looked about at the dim silhouettes of the mountains and saw only a crescent moon hanging alone in the heavens; a chill rose on every side, and in that clear solitude, with no one else in sight, I could not help feeling the same desolate wonder as in the old lines: "Beneath the pines I asked the boy; he said his master had gone to gather herbs, only somewhere on this mountain, hidden too deep in cloud to know where."

en: Where the realm exists, words exist

points.zh:
Aoraki / Mount Cook National Park 位於紐西蘭南島中部山脈脊幹，境内雪峰連嶂，有20多座3000公尺以上的高峰，境内40%是冰原冰川，加上縱谷溪流錯綜，氣勢壯麗雄偉，
故又稱爲南方的阿爾卑斯山脉。其中Mt. Cook高3754公尺 ( 12316呎 ) 是紐西蘭的最高峰。紐西蘭原住民毛利人 ( Maori ) 呌這座高山爲Aoraki，意謂揷雲山 ( Cloud Piercer )。境内也有紐西蘭最長的冰川，21公里的Tasman Glacier。夏日季節，斜坡平野綴滿百合，雛菊等野花，繽紛色澤漫延。1769年庫克船長登陸紐西蘭，1953年成立國家公園，1990年列入聯合國自然遺產名單。
points.en:
Aoraki / Mount Cook National Park is located along the central mountain spine of New Zealand's South Island, where snow-capped peaks stand in ranks, including more than 20 summits over 3,000 meters. Forty percent of the park is covered by ice fields and glaciers, and combined with its intricate network of valleys and streams, the scenery is magnificent and grand -- hence it is also known as the Southern Alps.
Mt. Cook, at 3,754 meters (12,316 feet), is the highest peak in New Zealand. The Maori, New Zealand's indigenous people, call this peak Aoraki, meaning "Cloud Piercer." The park is also home to New Zealand's longest glacier, the 21-kilometer Tasman Glacier. In summer, the slopes and plains are dotted with lilies, daisies, and other wildflowers, spreading a profusion of color across the land. Captain Cook landed in New Zealand in 1769; the national park was established in 1953, and in 1990 it was inscribed on the UN list of natural World Heritage sites.

points.zh:
「 尋隱者不遇 」:  " 松下問童子，言師採藥去，只在此山中，雲深不知處 " 是唐朝詩人賈島 ( 779年 - 840 年 ) 的代表作品。賈島是 " 苦吟派 " 詩人，著名的典故 「 推敲 」即出自此人。傳說他在驢背上苦思 「 鳥宿池邊樹，僧敲月下門 」 两句，反覆斟酌用推還是用敲字，以至錯入了韓愈的儀仗。韓愈建議用敲字，因敲字有聲，在深夜裡，增加了      静中有動的韻律。自己也說這两句是「二句三年得，一吟雙淚流 」，後來人們將斟酌選詞用字，遇事反覆思考稱作「 推敲 」。
賈島這首「 尋隱者不遇 」有隱逸詩最常用的素材，卽松和雲，也藉由松雲和童子，營造出 " 一問三答而無解答 " 恍惚飄渺的禪境和禪思。這首詩也藴含著中國古典詩中應用的 "空間的擴張 "，卽詩的畫面，由近而遠，由小而大，使視野越來越大，最後進入廣漠境界中。第一句的 " 松下 "，是局部原點，第二句的 " 採藥去 "，是由松下延伸到採藥的路上，是線的延伸，第三句的 " 山中 "，是面的層次，第四句 " 雲深不知處 "，則是面的無限擴大。 全詩由點而線而面，逐次擴展，以致於廣茫，而有 " 言有窮而意無盡 " 的韻味。
points.en:
"Visiting a Hermit and Not Finding Him": "Beneath the pine I asked the boy; he said his master had gone to gather herbs. He is somewhere within these mountains, but the clouds are deep and I do not know where" is the representative work of the Tang-dynasty poet Jia Dao (779-840). Jia Dao was a poet of the "painstaking chanting" school; the famous story of "tui qiao" ("push or knock") originates with him. Legend has it that, riding on his donkey, he pondered deeply over the two lines "The birds roost in the trees by the pond; a monk knocks at the gate beneath the moon," repeatedly weighing whether to use "push" or "knock," so absorbed that he wandered by mistake into Han Yu's honor-guard procession. Han Yu suggested using "knock," since the word produces a sound, and in the depths of night this adds a rhythm of motion within stillness. Jia Dao himself said of these two lines, "Two lines took three years to complete; a single recitation brings tears to both eyes." Later, people came to call the process of deliberating over word choice "tui qiao."
Jia Dao's "Visiting a Hermit and Not Finding Him" uses the most common materials of reclusion poetry—namely, pines and clouds—and through the pine, the clouds, and the boy, it creates the hazy, elusive Chan (Zen) mood and contemplation of "one question, three answers, and yet no resolution." This poem also embodies the technique of "spatial expansion" found in classical Chinese poetry—that is, the visual scope of the poem widens from near to far, from small to large, so that the field of view grows ever wider, finally entering into a vast, boundless realm. The "beneath the pine" of the first line is a localized point of origin; the "gone to gather herbs" of the second line extends from beneath the pine onto the road of gathering herbs, a linear extension; the "in the mountains" of the third line is a plane, a further layer; and the "the clouds are deep, I do not know where" of the fourth line is the infinite expansion of that plane. The whole poem expands from point to line to plane, growing broader and broader until it reaches a vast expanse, achieving the flavor of "words that end, yet meaning that never ends."
